{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — E-Path FX Licence Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Verified playbook findings and negotiation priorities

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement. Of 18 rules assessed, **12 are open** (9 deviations, 3 missing clauses) and **6 are compliant**. The risk profile is heavily one-sided in the Licensor's favour.

Three issues are critical and, in our view, must be resolved before signature:

- **Indemnification** — Article XII is a one-way indemnity running only from us to Licensor, and Article XIII expressly excludes any Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement claims. There is no Licensor indemnity anywhere in the document.
- **IP and data ownership** — Licensor owns the Licensed Technology and, through the "Derivative Work" definition, the bespoke customization and client front end we commission and pay for under Article VII(b). The Agreement is silent on ownership of our trading, order, client and account data.
- **Limitation of liability** — the cap protects only Licensor and is set at one half of amounts paid, while our liability is uncapped and expanded by the Article XII indemnity. There are no carve-outs of any kind.

Compounding these, we have **no exit**: the term is 36 months, renewal is at Licensor's unilateral option for a further seven years, there is no termination for convenience, no performance warranty (the platform is supplied wholly "AS IS"), no transition assistance or data-return right, and no vendor insurance. Assignment is barred for us with no successor carve-out while Licensor may assign freely, and a Licensee change of control automatically terminates the Agreement absent consent.

On the positive side, the Agreement imposes **no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum volume commitment, no MFN and no liquidated damages** on us; pricing is genuinely usage-based; and governing law and venue (New York law, exclusive New York courts) match our preferred position.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Arts. XII–XIII) |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (Art. III; defs. 1.2, 1.3, 1.6) |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. XIII) |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | General Provisions, § (c) Assignment; Arts. XX, XXII |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (Art. VI; General Provisions § (c); Art. XX) |
| 6 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (Arts. IV, XIX–XXI, XXIII) |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions |
| 8 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Arts. IV, V, XXI, XXIII) |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (def. 1.5; Arts. II, X) |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | Art. II.IV(b) (fee schedule / audit cost allocation) |
| 11 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. X(b)) |
| 12 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (Art. IV) |
| 13 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. XXI, Effect of Termination) |
| 14 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | Warranty Disclaimer (Art. VIX; Art. VII) |
| 15 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | General Provisions |
| 16 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (fee schedule; Art. XXII) |
| 17 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (fee schedule) |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | General Provisions |

### Notes on the compliant items

- **Exclusivity / non-compete / minimum commitment / MFN:** nothing in the Agreement restricts our sourcing, volume or pricing behaviour. The licence is expressly non-exclusive and fees are a tiered per-US$1m rate on actual traded volume, with higher volume reducing the rate. No redlines proposed.
- **Liquidated damages:** no penalty, shortfall or early-termination fee is payable by us; Article XXIII bars termination damages for both parties. The audit cost-shift (triggered only above a 5% discrepancy) is a cost-reimbursement mechanic, not a penalty.
- **Governing law:** New York law with exclusive New York courts, no arbitration clause. Venue is framed as the City of New York rather than New York County — noted only, not redlined.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following sit at or near the playbook's walk-away positions and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **No Licensor indemnity plus a one-way Licensee indemnity** (Arts. XII–XIII). Article XIII also expressly excludes Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement, so any indemnity we insert must override it. Fallback available: customary infringement exclusions with a 3x annual fees super-cap.
2. **Licensor-only liability cap at one half of amounts paid, with our liability uncapped and no carve-outs** (Art. XIII). Fallback: mutual 12-month cap with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
3. **Automatic termination on our change of control** (Art. XX), with consent deemed reasonably refused wherever Licensor believes its interests are affected — combined with a blanket bar on our assignment, no successor carve-out, unrestricted Licensor assignment, and a Licensor right of first refusal over our M&A (Art. XXII). Fallback: mutual assignment to successors on written notice.
4. **No Licensee termination for convenience** across a 36-month term. Fallback: 60–90 days' notice with fees capped at three months.
5. **Licensor's unilateral seven-year renewal option** (Art. IV), which we cannot decline and which is uncapped on price — and which conflicts with the mutual-written-agreement mechanic in Arts. IV.II and IV.III. Fallback: 60-day opt-out, uplift capped at 5%.
6. **Full "AS IS" supply with no conformance warranty and no remedy** (Art. VIX). Fallback: 90 days software / 30 days services with repair, replace or refund.
7. **No data return or transition assistance** (Art. XXI). Article XXI is entirely one-directional: we must return everything within five days with officer certification, while all Licensor rights survive. Our order, trade and account records sit on Licensor's hosted systems with no contractual right of recovery. Fallback: 90 days' assistance with a 30-day export.
8. **Unlimited audit frequency** (Art. II.IV(b)). Other elements already meet our preferred position (independent mutually agreed CPA, records-only scope, 30 days' lead time, Licensor-borne cost below a 5% discrepancy); only frequency, business hours and auditor confidentiality need fixing. Fallback: once per year.
9. **Non-solicitation of all Licensor personnel for the Term plus three years, binding us only** (Art. X(b)), backed by injunctive relief. Fallback: mutual, personnel directly involved, 12 months from end of involvement.
10. **No vendor insurance** for a vendor hosting the platform and processing our data. Fallback: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Confirm the walk-away list with the business.** Items 1–7 above are structural; we recommend the deal team confirm whether the trading benefit justifies proceeding if Licensor refuses movement on indemnity, liability cap and exit.
2. **Issue the redline** covering the nine deviations and three missing clauses, in the priority order: (i) Licensor IP/misconduct indemnity and narrowing of our Article XII indemnity; (ii) mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000 with uncapped Excluded Claims and confirmation that our fee obligations are not capped "damages"; (iii) our retention of our data and assignment of paid-for customization deliverables, with a licence-back of embedded Licensor IP and no joint ownership.
3. **Then the exit and term package:** Licensee termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with refund of prepaid fees; mutual 12-month renewals with 30-day opt-out and CPI/3% uplift cap conformed to the existing mutual-agreement language in Arts. IV.II–IV.III; transition assistance (up to six months) and data return in machine-readable format within 30 days with certified deletion, inserted as a new Art. XXI(c).
4. **Then the remaining asks:** affiliate/contractor extension of the licence grant and consent-free successor transfer; affiliate/successor assignment carve-out with a mutual reasonable-consent standard and a bar on Licensor assigning to our competitors; express 12-month conformance warranty carved out of the disclaimer; audit capped at once per 12 months on 30 days' notice during business hours with the auditor under confidentiality; mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to involved personnel (retaining the existing advertising/unsolicited-inquiry carve-out); and vendor insurance as a new General Provisions sub-clause.
5. **Note for the record, not redlined here:** the Article XXII right of first refusal over a sale or merger of the Company. It is not an exclusivity or MFN restriction, but it constrains our exit flexibility alongside Article XX and should be raised commercially.
6. **Note also:** there is no service-credit or other vendor-side performance remedy running to us. That is outside the rules assessed, but worth raising if the business relies on platform availability.

Please confirm the walk-away list and we will circulate the redline and cover comments to Licensor's counsel."}
